stem: Your team requires that every file Claude Code writes is automatically checked by a formatter — with no exceptions, even if nobody asks for it. Which mechanism fits best?
opciones: A skill with a description mentioning "format files"
A PostToolUse hook matching Write/Edit tool calls
A CLAUDE.md rule stating "always format files"
A subagent dedicated to formatting
explicacion: B. "Automatically… no exceptions… even if nobody asks" = evento + garantía = hook (PostToolUse sobre Write/Edit). Una skill (A) y CLAUDE.md (C) dependen del criterio de Claude — probabilístico; el subagent (D) no automatiza nada.

stem: You clone a team repository that ships a code-review skill in .claude/skills/. You already have a personal code-review skill in ~/.claude/skills/. When you ask for a review, whose instructions apply?
opciones: The project skill — project settings are more specific than personal ones
The personal skill — personal has higher priority than project
Both are merged into one combined instruction set
Neither — Claude reports a conflict and asks you to choose
explicacion: B. Prioridad E-P-P-P: Enterprise → Personal → Project → Plugins. La trampa es A ("más específico"): la intuición falla, Personal gana a Project. No hay merge (C) ni diálogo de conflicto (D).

stem: At startup, what does Claude Code load into context from each available skill?
opciones: The full SKILL.md file of every skill
Only the name and description fields
The frontmatter plus the first 500 lines
Nothing — skills are only discovered when a request matches
explicacion: B. Solo name + description — la base de la eficiencia de contexto. D describe mal el mecanismo: la lista SÍ se precarga, porque sin ella no habría contra qué hacer el matching.

stem: A SKILL.md frontmatter contains only name and description. What can Claude do with tools while this skill is active?
opciones: Nothing — without allowed-tools, the skill cannot use any tools
Only read-only tools like Read and Grep
Anything its normal permission model allows — omitting allowed-tools means no restriction
Only the tools mentioned inside the skill's instructions
explicacion: C. Omitir allowed-tools = sin restricción (modelo de permisos normal). A es la trampa clásica: "omitido" NO significa "sin herramientas".

stem: Your skill's SKILL.md has grown to 1,900 lines, mostly large reference tables that only matter for rare edge cases. Following the open standard, what should you do?
opciones: Split it into two skills with different names
Move the tables to references/ files and link them from SKILL.md with an explicit "only load when..." condition
Raise the skill's model field so a larger model can handle the content
Compress the tables into shorter prose to fit under 500 lines
explicacion: B. Progressive disclosure: SKILL.md < 500 líneas como índice + references/ con condición explícita "Only load when…". D pierde contenido; A fragmenta sin necesidad. No se recorta material: se decide CUÁNDO entra.

stem: A skill includes a 300-line validation script in scripts/. What instruction should SKILL.md contain so the script stays context-efficient, and why?
opciones: "Read the script before running it" — so Claude understands what it does
"Run the script, not read it" — execution only puts the script's output into context
"Summarize the script" — a summary is cheaper than the full file
"Inline the script's logic into SKILL.md" — instructions are cheaper than code
explicacion: B. "Tell Claude to run the script, not read it" — al ejecutar, solo el output consume tokens (300 líneas de código → quizá 3 de salida). Además el código probado es determinista.

stem: A financial company must guarantee that a security-review skill is applied consistently by every developer, and that no developer can override it with their own version. Which distribution method?
opciones: Commit the skill to each team repository
Publish it as a plugin on an internal marketplace
Deploy it via enterprise managed settings
Email the skill folder to all developers to install personally
explicacion: C. Keyword "must" + "no developer can override" = enterprise managed settings: prioridad máxima, pisa cualquier skill del mismo nombre. Repo (A) y plugin (B) quedan por debajo de Personal en prioridad.

stem: You create a custom subagent in .claude/agents/reviewer.md and expect it to use your accessibility-audit skill, but it never applies it. What is the most likely cause?
opciones: The subagent's model field is set too low
Skills must be listed explicitly in the agent's skills: frontmatter field — subagents don't inherit skills
The skill needs allowed-tools to work inside subagents
Subagents can only use enterprise skills
explicacion: B. El gotcha: los subagents no heredan skills — nacen con contexto limpio; hay que listarlas en skills:. Y recuerda: los built-in (Explore, Plan, Verify) no pueden usarlas en absoluto.

stem: A skill exists, passes the validator, and appears in the available skills list — but Claude never uses it when you ask in your usual way. Per the course, what is the cause "almost always," and the fix?
opciones: A priority conflict — rename the skill
The description lacks overlap with how you phrase requests — add real trigger phrases
A YAML syntax error — re-run the validator
The skill is too long — apply progressive disclosure
explicacion: B. "The cause is almost always the description" — falta overlap semántico; agrega las frases que TÚ realmente usas y prueba variaciones ("why is this slow?", "make this faster").

stem: A skill loads fine but its script fails at runtime on Windows. Which pair of fixes does the course recommend?
opciones: Rename SKILL.md to skill.md and restart
Move the script to assets/ and reference it from the description
Give scripts execute permission (chmod +x) and use forward slashes ( / ) in all paths
Reinstall Claude Code and clear the plugin cache
explicacion: C. Runtime errors: chmod +x a los scripts + forward slashes ( / ) incluso en Windows (+ dependencias instaladas y anotadas en la description).
